correctness.rationale: The two attachment vertices are same-colored by the end-interchanging graph automorphism, and all other degree-two vertices lie on threads of lengths m or p between degree-three endpoints in the universal cover. At round r, each thread position has color determined by unordered clipped distances from its endpoints; induction extends one visible edge per round, with degree-three endpoint color as anchor. Same-thread partitions stabilize at floor(L/2). Unequal thread lengths first separate positions near an endpoint at round min(m,p), while equal threads remain identified forever. If p!=m, position up to reflection and thread type exactly describes automorphism orbits; if p=m, connector internal vertices are cut vertices while cycle internal vertices are not, proving orbit mismatch. Independently reimplemented 1-WL and constructed graphs for all 210 pairs 3<=m<=12, 0<=k<=20 and reproduced the depth formula, including 10 resonances. Infinite claim relies on clipped-distance induction, not these samples.

final_claim: For equal-cycle dumbbell graphs D_{m,k,m}, m>=3,k>=0, p=k+1, color-refinement depth from uniform colors equals floor(m/2) when p=m and otherwise max(floor(m/2),ceil(k/2),min(m,p)). Stable colors recover automorphism orbits iff p!=m; resonance p=m leaves cycle and connector positions color-equivalent but nonautomorphic.
